observations:
Torah #181 contains 2 bechina edges in the dataset, yielding 1 package of 3 nodes (יעקב, כבוד, נפש — Package 1: יַעֲקֹב וְהַכָּבוֹד). The framework threshold for a new package is '3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain.' All 3 bechina-connected concepts are already assigned to Package 1.

The remaining concepts in the teaching — קֶשֶׁר, חֶלְקֵי הַכָּבוֹד, גַּדְלוּת/קַטְנוּת, רְשָׁעִים, חִיּוּת מֵהַנֶּפֶשׁ, תַּאֲוַת נִאוּף, נְפִילָה, מַחֲלֹקֶת קֹרַח, צַדִּיק הָאֱמֶת — are all connected to the teaching exclusively through eitza (causal) relationships. None of these concepts is declared a bechina of any other concept within Torah #181.

Assessment of potential independent domains:

1. Evil mirror (conspiracy/lust cluster): The concepts קֶשֶׁר, נְפִילָה, and תַּאֲוַת נִיאוּף form a causal chain (conspiracy → fall → lust). While these three concepts operate together as the 'evil pole' of the teaching, they are linked by eitza (cause-effect), not bechina (shared nature). The text never says 'niuf is a bechina of nefilah' or 'kesher is a bechina of niuf.' Eitza chains cannot constitute packages (framework rule 3.2: 'packages are formed from bechina-connected nodes, not eitza edges'). No package can be proposed from this cluster.

2. Honor mechanics cluster (chelkei kavod, gadlut/katnut): These are quantitative sub-aspects of kavod, used illustratively in the eitza chain. They do not form an independent domain with bechina connections among themselves.

Conclusion: Torah #181 is a teaching with a minimal bechina layer (one triad: יעקב–כבוד–נפש) and a rich eitza argument (the conspiracy-honor-fall dynamic). The single package (Package 1) captures all bechina content. No additional packages — new or otherwise — are warranted.
